purpose: Demonstrate typed native state transitions in isolated real Excel and Blender sessions before attaching human input or cross-application actions.

activities.label: create observe mutate and revert isolated native Excel and Blender states
attack user file physical input network and nonreversible transition boundaries
record typed transition kernel and remaining human input unknowns

queries.expression: can real Excel and Blender expose create select modify and revert transitions in isolated unsaved sessions
does a typed transition kernel preserve more meaning than a button or coordinate mapping
does the probe avoid user files physical input camera screenshot network and source writes
is the transition probe registered and reproducible in the FARMAKSIA suite

assumptions: The isolated Excel DispatchEx process starts with no user workbook attached.
Blender factory-startup background mode has no user scene that needs preservation.
In-memory scratch mutation is allowed when no user file is opened or saved.
A common kernel can describe compatible transitions without claiming application equivalence.
Human input will be attached only after the native state deltas are observable.
kill_tests: Writing a user file is blocked.
Physical keyboard or mouse injection is blocked.
Network, screenshot and camera capabilities are blocked.
Replacing a typed transition with a click-button mapping is blocked.
Replacing revert with a dirty non-reversible state is blocked.
unknowns: Whether UIA can identify the same semantic target that the native API identifies.
Whether a human input trace can be decoded into the common kernel without capturing private content.
Whether a task transition in Excel has a useful analogue in Blender beyond the four primitives.
Whether an independent verifier can observe future real user actions without using the same adapter.
